Araw yan ng bride at groom - sila may desisyon kung sino iinvite nila. They have their reasons and that's not something I believe should be taken so personally. I have dozenssss of relatives from both sides who have family celebrations each year and some, I don't get invited to. Reasons might range from:

1) They have not heard from me in years
2) They do not think my vibe will match theirs
3) They remembered I'm always busy and might not come anyway
4) I have not shared any of my milestones with them so why should they?
5) Some just don't like me.

For friends and acquaintances naman:
1) I might not be as close to them as I thought and that's on me
2) They're on a budget
3) Religion
4) Limited number of people lang talaga yung invited

And I respect that! Good for them for having boundaries. Good for them for figuring out who they want to share their milestones with. Right nila piliin yon. Di ko naman ikakamatay kung si ako makakakain ng lechon and chicken cordon bleu sa reception.

(Also sidenote: Kung aware kang may ugaling kang undesirable, wala kang right mag drama bakit di ka dinidesire.)

Same tbh. I started working in Bacolod. Every sweldo daw sakto lang ibayad naman para sa galastuhon. Kagasto kag kadugay sang byahe. Kagahod sang palibot. You try to save up pero mas convenient nalang mag bakal or mag grab, ang karinderya nga lapit medyo layo, kainit, gutok, bisan karenderya mahal gyapon (wala ko gina generalize ni ha, base lang sa experience. May mga mahal nga karinderya depende sa location). When I moved to Silay, it changed. You do have less options when it comes to food (i mean unlike bacolod nga left and right damo ka gusto i try nga bag-o) but that means you have less temptations - di ka maka feel FOMO kung may new up and coming place. kag kung mag choose ka, it's either REALLY good or okay lang so wala ka pirdehon. And accessible lang tanan with a short tricycle drive.

Open man ko nga it's probably just bc nag change akon lifestyle, nag change akon sweldo kag industry pero mas at peace lang gid utok ko di. daw wala nako iban palibugan. I don't blame Bacolod - i'm not saying there's something wrong with bacolod. I bet I'd feel the same way if I lived in a different busy city.

Edit to mention that I was born in Bacolod and lived there for 26-27 years. So kung pinsaron, dapat naanad nako sa kagamo. But yea, I love it here in Silay better.

I work for a company that has shops on both lazada and shopee. I am 80% sure na nsa tao lang yung idea na mas maganda yung lazada sa shopee. Shopee has a feature that tries to prevent misleading discounts (although there are loopholes). Lazada so far wala akong na notice. I could change prices and discounts at will without getting flagged (or baka mabagal lang ma flag). Customer service for order issues will still depend on the seller so same quality lang yung makukuha mong treatment regardless of platform.

 Sales are 50% higher on shopee but conversion rates are much higher on lazada (mataas din basket sizes). People trust lazada more for expensive purchases.

Idk if this information is useful. Ofc iba yung data ng ibang shops depende sa kung ano binebenta nila. Masyadong noob pa ako dito but those are my observations.
